text:
Maya: ran a focused benchmark sweep this morning across A100/H100/L40S — wanted to flag a weird kernel fallback pattern and KV cache thrash.
ops-bot: uploaded run artifacts: https://redwood-internal/perf/2100012345 :file_folder: (seq sweep + batch sweep)
Eli: quick summary pls — is this the hybrid fused/paged run? :eyes:
Maya: yes — we tested three variants: native Flash, paged-attn (4k pages), and fused-paged hybrid (split op at seq boundary). swept seq len = [128,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768] and batch = [1,2,4,8,16,32] on each GPU.
Arpan: what stands out?
Maya: two things: 1) on H100 the kernel_selector v2.7 flips from fused->paged at seq 4096 for batch>=8, but P95 jumps ~12% compared to v2.6. 2) on L40S we see KV cache page reallocation spikes when batch>16 for long seqs causing tail latency spikes.
Jen: do you have exact numbers?
Maya: pasted minimal table from the run: 
```
H100 fused-hybrid P50/P95 (seq=8192,b=8): 85ms / 210ms
H100 paged P50/P95 (seq=8192,b=8): 92ms / 235ms
H100 fused (v2.6) P50/P95 (seq=8192,b=8): 78ms / 188ms
L40S fused P95 (seq=16384,b=16): 410ms (KV page thrash observed)
```
Eli: so v2.7 selector favors paged at that point which increased latency vs v2.6 fused — sounds like fallback criteria too eager.
Arpan: any perf counter traces? cache miss rate, page fault counts?
Maya: yes — trace shows page_alloc_count spikes at the same time as p95 spikes, and sustained memcpy stalls. I'll attach flame traces in the artifact.
Kai: could this be input distribution skew — more long sequences for certain batches?
Maya: we used synthetic uniform seq distribution for sweep to isolate behavior. not skew.
Jen: reproduction command?
Maya: run in bench dir: `./run_attn_sweep --device H100 --model l40s-8bit --seq 8192 --batch 8 --variant fused-hybrid --kernel-selector v2.7 --trace perf.json`
Eli: suggestion: add a hysteresis to selector: require sustained performance delta for 3 consecutive windows before switching kernel. also consider preferring fused for quantized L40S up to 16k since we see fewer memcpy stalls.
Arpan: +1. also add a soft-limit on concurrent page_allocs to avoid thrash — allocate page pool upfront for long-seq heavy batches.
Maya: experimented with prealloc pool of pages=64 on L40S and p95 dropped ~22% for seq>=16k, batch 16. tradeoff is commit memory.
Kai: any regression risk? changing selector hysteresis could keep suboptimal kernel longer. we need a quick AB test.
Maya: set up canary config: selector.hysteresis=3 windows + prealloc for longseq; canary on 10% of traffic dedicated to longseq profile. will run on staging cluster tomorrow.
Jen: nits — log the selector decision with windowed metrics and export to console dashboard so SRE can see flips.
Eli: also add a debug flag to force_fused/force_paged for quick rollback during incidents.
Maya: noted. I'll open a PR with the selector patch + L40S prealloc change and include benchmark harness and reproducer.
Arpan: probs worth pinning default selector to v2.6 for the next tenant-facing deploy until we validate v2.7 changes.
Maya: agree — will mark rollout blocked until canary completes or we revert.
ops-bot: incident policy: rollout_blocked created by Maya for kernel-selector v2.7 at 2100012400 :warning:
Eli: thanks — good catch. will help triage the PR. :thumbsup:
